summary: The candidate captures the paper's main geometric-to-algebraic-to-RT construction and most foundational definitions, with generally accurate pages and broadly appropriate entry classes. Its principal defect is pervasive mathematical text corruption: many formulas have lost LaTeX commands or operators, and several occurrences of the essential symbol ±1 have become the mathematically false value 71. It also promotes a bibliography/attribution summary to a theorem and omits several Gold supporting entries as distinct mathematical units. The extraction is therefore structurally useful but requires substantial formula repair before it can be treated as a reliable mathematical artifact.
strengths: Covers the central chain from framed-link surgery and Kirby calculus through ribbon categories, ribbon Hopf algebras, modular data, Kirby color, normalization, and the Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant.

Includes the principal results: Lickorish–Wallace, Kirby calculus, the Turaev ribbon-graph functor, the ribbon structure on finite-dimensional representations, purification, and the final RT invariance theorem.
Captures important supporting notions such as categorical and quantum traces, negligible modules, modular Hopf algebras, handle-slide invariance, and the surgery normalization formula.
Entry types are mostly sensible, and the reported page locators are generally consistent with the embedded source text.

Several additional source-grounded entries, including Rohlin cobordism, Yang–Baxter, the pivotal element, and the Jones/WRT specialization discussion, add legitimate coverage beyond the Gold reference.
issues: There is pervasive malformed mathematics caused by dropped backslashes and OCR substitutions, including strings such as `cucdotscu`, `ldots`, `cal V`, `race{V_ir`, `xtimes`, `ci`, `in`, and `tau` appearing as plain letters rather than valid LaTeX commands.

The blackboard-framing entry says that a curl changes writhe by `$71$` rather than $\pm1$, and the Kirby-calculus theorem similarly replaces a $\pm1$-framed unknot by a `71`-framed unknot. These are substantive mathematical errors in foundational entries.
The Lickorish–Wallace statement has corrupted union, ellipsis, framing, and homeomorphism notation, weakening the precision of a core theorem.

Many otherwise correct entries have unbalanced or semantically broken formulas, especially the ribbon-category, Yang–Baxter, dual-module, RT-invariant, modular-category, modular-Hopf, and quantum-group entries.
The entry `paper:theorem:external-rt-source` is not a mathematical theorem; it is a bibliographic attribution summary and should be classified as a remark, fact, or metadata record.

External attribution is inconsistent: some externally sourced theorems are explicitly marked `external`, while Lickorish–Wallace, Rohlin, and Kirby calculus are not marked consistently in the final entries.

Several Gold supporting entries are not represented as distinct entries, notably the general Hopf-algebra definition, standalone twist definition, finite simple-system/domination definition, standalone Hopf-link matrix definition, negligible-morphism and purification definitions, the blow-up invariance lemma, Kirby reduction, and surgery-presentation independence.

Some Gold lemmas are absorbed into definitions rather than extracted as claims, including coproduct-induced monoidality, antipode-induced duality, R-matrix braiding, and universal-twist compatibility. This preserves much of the content but reduces entry-level structural fidelity.
The graphical-calculus item is typed as `algorithm`; while understandable, the Gold treats this material as definitional infrastructure, so its classification is not fully aligned.

The assertion in the Rohlin entry that the bounding four-manifold may be required to be a $2$-handlebody is stronger than the basic cobordism statement and belongs more naturally to the surgery theorem discussion.

entryLevelComparison.assessment: The framing definition is substantially correct and located on page 2, but it is stated first for a link and then specializes the integer description to a knot rather than explicitly assigning an integer to every component of a framed link.
Faithfully captures the $2$-handlebody construction and the boundary surgery manifold, with only minor formatting issues.
The intended theorem and page are correct, but central notation for the link, framings, surgery manifold, and equivalence is badly mangled.
Correctly identifies the theorem and its other moves, but replaces the essential $\pm1$-framed unknot move with a `71`-framed unknot.
Contains the correct conceptual data and compatibility conditions, but the formulas are heavily damaged by lost LaTeX commands.
Accurately states the existence and closed-graph value of the ribbon-graph functor, including the scalar-valued specialization.
Correctly classifies and states the ribbon structure on finite-dimensional representations of a ribbon Hopf algebra.
The categorical/quantum trace identification is present, supported by a separate quantum-trace definition, but its notation is not consistently valid LaTeX.
All four substantive modular-category conditions are present, but widespread token corruption makes the displayed statement unreliable as mathematical text.
Captures the Kirby-color handle-slide property and its dependence on nondegenerate modular data.
Gives the intended RT surgery normalization and useful normalizations for $S^3$ and $S^1\times S^2$; the stored JSON statement has valid delimiters here.
Invariance under all Kirby moves is asserted in the final theorem, but the separate $\pm1$ blow-up normalization lemma is not extracted.
The full intended conclusion, including the pair invariant, is present, but almost every important mathematical symbol in the statement is malformed.
The purification operation and its modular-category outcome appear inside the theorem, but no standalone definition of purification or negligible morphisms is extracted.
The unit, duality, decomposition modulo negligible modules, and invertible monodromy matrix conditions are all covered, but the formula notation is extensively damaged.
The cited references are relevant, but a statement that the paper attributes constructions to these sources is bibliographic metadata rather than a theorem.
